I'm 63 this year, been farming these 4 mu of land in Quzhou for 40 years now. My husband passed a few years back, so mostly it's me at home — our son works construction in Handan and sends some money when he can, but I can't count on that for buying fertilizer. I finished middle school, so I can read the bags and understand what the extension people say, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some young technician tells me.

I split my land about 60/40: about **2 and a half mu** for the wheat-corn rotation, and about **1 and a half mu** for cotton. The grain is for food security — we need that wheat and corn. Cotton gives cash, but it's more work and more risk at my age.

**Winter wheat** is already in the ground — I planted the 2.5 mu last October, same as always. I put down base fertilizer then, about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's late April and the wheat is at jointing. I need to topdress with urea soon. The extension station says 15 kg N per mu is enough, but last year I did closer to 18 kg total and the yield was better than my neighbor who skimped. So I'll topdress with about 10 kg urea per mu now. Pumping water costs about 30 yuan each time, so I have to watch it — I'll irrigate this week at jointing, and probably twice more if it's dry: once at flowering and maybe once at grain filling. I sprayed herbicide in early spring, and I'll keep an eye out for aphids. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather holds. That's not great, but this soil is getting tired and I can't afford to push it harder.

**Summer maize** comes right after wheat harvest in early June. That window is brutal — sometimes only 5 days between cutting wheat and getting corn in the ground. I'll buy hybrid seed from Old Wang's shop in the village, about 3 kg per mu, costs around 30 yuan. I'll hire the tractor for planting since I don't have my own — that's another 40 yuan per mu. I'll put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 30 kg per mu, and then topdress with urea at the big flare stage if the plants look hungry — maybe another 10 kg per mu. For water, if the summer rains are normal I might only need to irrigate once, maybe twice. I don't spray much for corn, just a herbicide right after planting. I expect about 450 kg per mu, about average for my land.

**Cotton** — I'm planting 1.6 mu this week. I saved some seed from last year but I always mix in some fresh seed from the shop. Never trust saved seed completely, it gets weak. Cotton needs a lot of labor, especially picking, and at 63 bending down all day is hard on my back. I'll put base fertilizer down at planting — compound fertilizer about 35 kg per mu — then topdress twice, at flowering and when the bolls are setting. I'll spray for bollworm three times, that's the main pest here, and irrigate twice if it doesn't rain. For picking in September and October, I'll do what I can myself, but I'll hire two women from the village for about 5 days total — that'll cost me about 100 yuan per day each. I expect about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton, though that depends a lot on the weather and pests.

Money is tight. I'm spending almost 1,800 yuan on inputs this year, which is most of my cash reserve. I thought about putting more land into wheat-corn because it's less risky, but cotton prices were decent last year and I need some cash income. If cotton fails, at least I have the grain. That's how I've survived 40 years — never put all your eggs in one basket, and never spend your last yuan.
